title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p4】Despite these insights, no study has directly isolated and optimized a culture system for intramuscular preadipocytes in rabbits, a methodological gap that is particularly critical given that rabbits exhibit unique metabolic characteristics as hindgut fermenters, distinct from both monogastric and ruminant species.17 Developing a reliable in vitro culture system for rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes (IMPA) would not only facilitate exploration of adipogenesis in this species but also enable investigation into the regulatory roles of lncRNAs, transcription factors, and microbiota-derived metabolites in IMF development. This methodological gap impedes mechanistic research on rabbit intramuscular adipogenesis and its implications for meat quality. To address this, our study was designed to establish and comprehensively characterize a standardized in vitro model system for rabbit IMPA. We specifically focus on developing a robust isolation and culture protocol from a neonatal source, ensuring a consistent and viable cell population for foundational studies. The primary aim is not to characterize the in vivo IMPA population at slaughter age, but to develop and validate an essential in vitro tool. By optimizing enzymatic digestion and culture conditions and providing comprehensive morphological and molecular validation (including the expression of key adipogenic markers), we establish the identity and adipogenic potential of rabbit IMPAs. This work lays critical groundwork for subsequent investigations into the molecular and nutritional regulation of IMF deposition in rabbits, offering a direct methodological foundation for meat science and genetic improvement strategies.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Traditionally, rabbit breeding focused on wool and fur production, utilizing breeds such as Angora and Rex.1 Recently, however, meat production has gained significance, particularly with the New Zealand and Californian breeds, due to the favourable nutritional profile of rabbit meat compared to that of conventional livestock.2 Rabbit meat is lean, contains lower overall fat, and has a beneficial fatty acid composition. Its MF is enriched with lecithin and unsaturated lipids, which enhance tenderness, juiciness, and flavor.3 These qualities have spurred interest in the biological mechanisms that regulate meat quality in rabbits.

Penicillin/streptomycin (double antibody), dexamethasone (DEX), insulin, type I and type II collagenase were purchased from Sanya Solebao Biotechnology Co., Ltd., Hainan Sheng, China. The Oil Red O staining kit was obtained from the Biosun company, China. The RNA extraction kit was acquired from Meiji Seika Pharma Co., Ltd., Japan, while reverse transcription and quantification kits were sourced from Takara, Dalian, China. sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Immunofluorescence validation of adipogenic markers in undifferentiated and differentiated preadipocytes · S0004-S2004-p1】Immunofluorescence staining was conducted on isolated stromal vascular cells under both undifferentiated and adipogenic differentiation conditions to examine the expression of key adipogenic markers, including leptin, PREF-1, and PPARγ, in rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes and to verify cell identity (Figure 4). The analysis revealed distinct stage-dependent differences in both the expression levels and subcellular localization of these markers between undifferentiated and early differentiated preadipocytes, consistent with progression toward the adipogenic lineage.

【Immunofluorescence validation of adipogenic markers in undifferentiated and differentiated preadipocytes · S0004-S2004-p2】In undifferentiated cells (Figure 4(a)), leptin exhibited minimal or absent CY3 fluorescence, indicating a lack of adipokine production characteristic of preadipocytes.34 In contrast, PREF-1 displayed a detectable cytoplasmic signal, consistent with its role as a preadipocyte-associated factor that maintains cells in an undifferentiated, anti-adipogenic state. PPARγ staining in undifferentiated cells was weak and largely non-nuclear, suggesting that the core adipogenic transcriptional program was not yet activated. Corresponding RT-qPCR analysis confirmed that basal PPARγ transcript levels were notably lower than those of the preadipocyte marker PREF-1 (Figure 3(d)), suggesting that most cells had not yet fully differentiated. The detection of nuclear PPARγ in preadipocytes aligns with its reported role in early adipogenic lineage priming and commitment.35

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Schematic workflow for the isolation and primary culture of intramuscular preadipocytes from neonatal hycole rabbit longissimus dorsi (LD) muscle.The LD muscle was aseptically dissected from 3-day-old rabbit kits. After washing in PBS containing 2% penicillin/streptomycin and removing the connective tissue, the muscle was minced into fragments of 1–3 mm³. Tissue fragments were enzymatically digested with type I collagenase (2 mg/mL) at 37 °C for 90 minutes. The digestion was neutralized with an equal volume of DMEM/F12 medium containing 10% FBS. The cell suspension was sequentially filtered through 70 µm and 40 µm cell strainers and then centrifuged at 1200 rpm for 10 minutes to obtain the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) pellet. The SVF was washed, resuspended, and plated in complete growth medium (DMEM high glucose, 15% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin). Adherent cells were cultured at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and expanded through passage 3 for downstream analysis.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Timeline of adipogenic induction in rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes.This schematic provides an overview of the differentiation protocol. Cells were cultured to 80–90% confluence by Day −2 and were then induced with adipogenic medium on Day 0. Maintenance medium was supplied on Day 2 and refreshed every 48 hours thereafter. Complete adipocyte differentiation was achieved by Day 12.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Cell morphology, proliferation ability, and gene expression of rabbit intramuscular preadipocyte. (a) Primary growth of preadipocytes in rabbit (12 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, and 72 hours post isolation. Scale bar: 200 µm (applies to all panels). (b) Relative expression levels of marker genes were compared between pure intramuscular fibroblasts (control) and the SVF-derived cell population suspected to be intramuscular preadipocytes. Genes assessed include: ITGA7 (myogenic progenitor marker), CD34 and PDGFRA (preadipocyte/stromal markers), ADIPOQ (mature adipocyte marker), and MYOD1 (myoblast marker). Low expression of fibroblast and myogenic markers (ITGA7, MYOD1) alongside elevated expression of preadipocyte markers (CD34, PDGFRA) in the SVF population supports successful isolation and purity of preadipocytes with minimal contamination from fibroblasts or myogenic cells. Data are presented as mean ± SEM. (c) growth curve of rabbit preadipocyte cell using CCK8; (d) The relative mRNA expression of key lineage-specific markers in passage 3 (P3) IMF-SVF-derived cells maintained in the undifferentiated, proliferative state before adipogenic induction . Expression levels (mean ± SEM) were normalized to β-actin and compared to a calibrator sample. The profile confirms that the isolated cells are preadipocytes, as indicated by high expression of adipogenic markers (PPARG, PREF1/DLK1, Zfp423, PDGFRA). The negligible expression of the hematopoietic marker PTPRC (CD45) confirms the absence of immune cell contamination. Additionally, low expression levels of myocyte (MYOD1), osteocyte (Pax7), fibroblast (COL1A1), and mature adipocyte (ADIPOQ, C/EBPa) markers further support the preadipocyte lineage commitment and the purity of the isolated cell population. Data were obtained from n = 3 independent biological replicates.
